## Context

<!--
The uncertainty or risk that motivates the spike, and the decision that stays
blocked until it is resolved. Name the decision explicitly — a spike that
unblocks nothing is reading, not work.
-->

## Questions to answer

<!--
Concrete and answerable with evidence, not opinion. Each one must have a
possible answer that would change what you build.

Good: "Does library X report values per item or in aggregate?"
Bad:  "Investigate library X."
-->

- [ ]
- [ ]

## Timebox

<!--
Hours or days. When it expires, report what was learned rather than extending
silently — an overrunning spike is itself a finding.
-->

## Deliverable

<!--
Where the answer lands: an ADR, a README section, a throwaway branch, a row in
the decision log. A spike delivers knowledge, not production code — if the
output is meant to ship, file a feat instead.
-->

## Findings

<!--
Filled in as the spike runs. Record what was ruled out as well as what was
chosen: the discarded options are the part nobody can reconstruct later.
-->

## Outcome

<!--
Completed at the end: the decision taken, and the issues it spawns.
-->
